journeys.description: Tap a pin shared by multiple Collection Entries → opens the LocationSheet listing all entries at that pin.
Tap a pin owned by exactly one Collection Entry → opens the EntrySheet for that entry.
Tap the Collections button in the MapOverview chrome → CollectionList.
Long-press the map to drop a pin → LocationDraftSheet with nearby resolution candidates.
Browse-mode pick of a provider candidate → LocationSheet showing the resolved Location with an empty entries list, where TAP_ADD_ENTRY is the next step into AddLocationToCollection.

Add-to-collection mode pick of a provider candidate → AddLocationToCollection with the candidate pre-filled and the originating Collection pre-selected (skips both LocationSheet and LocationDraftSheet). Mode-only journey: meaningful only when MapOverview carries a collection-context.
Tap the Settings affordance → Settings surface.
In addToCollection mode, dismiss the status bar → return to CollectionDetail. Mode-only journey: meaningful only when MapOverview carries a collection-context.

Tap a single-entry pin, then hand off the Location to the system maps app. OPEN_EXTERNALLY lands on ExternalApp — a non-app surface representing the OS-level handoff. The chart does not declare OPEN_EXTERNALLY on EntrySheet, nor does it model ExternalApp as a surface — the verifier will report both as chart-missing / unknown-surface. EntrySheet's meta.actions also lacks Location.openExternally; that affordance gap belongs to doc02.02.02.09.

Tap a single-entry pin, edit the Review, save, and land back on EntrySheet with a top snackbar acknowledging the save. Currently SUBMIT targets CollectionEntryDetail (target-mismatch) — for map-rooted edits, returning to EntrySheet preserves the user's map context. The post-submit snackbar context on EntrySheet is a new affordance analogous to MapOverview's pending-review-context.
Tap a multi-entry pin, then pick which Collection's Entry to peek at. Extends tap-pin-multi by one step; shares its prefix and diverges only after LocationSheet.

User intent: drop a pin, add it to a Collection, then review it. PICK_COLLECTION lands on MapOverview (showing a transient 'go to review' status bar — a mode of MapOverview, not a separate state). Tapping that bar fires GO_TO_REVIEW → ReviewForm. The statechart does not yet expose GO_TO_REVIEW; the verifier reports it as chart-missing.

Create a new Collection from scratch. CollectionEditor's DONE steps back one surface to CollectionList, which surfaces a snackbar carrying the just-created Collection; tapping VIEW_NEW_COLLECTION on the snackbar opens that Collection's CollectionDetail. The post-save snackbar context on CollectionList is a new affordance analogous to MapOverview's pending-review-context. Currently the chart's DONE targets CollectionDetail (target-mismatch) and does not declare VIEW_NEW_COLLECTION (chart-missing); the verifier will surface both.

Tap a single-entry pin to open EntrySheet, then tap the locationBlock to see the Location surface (LocationSheet) — the skinny peek of that Location and any sibling Entries. The peek renders for any Entry count, so on a single-entry pin it is a one-row list above the *Add another Entry at this Location* affordance — the launching pad for binding a sibling Entry without leaving the map context.

From a single-entry pin, peek the Location and bind a new Entry to the same Location. Opens EntrySheet, pivots to LocationSheet via TAP_LOCATION, then TAP_ADD_ENTRY hands off to AddLocationToCollection with the existing Location carried as `location-context`. PICK_COLLECTION commits the new Entry against the chosen Collection and returns to MapOverview with the just-created Entry as `pending-review-context`.
Tap a single-entry pin to open EntrySheet, then tap the collectionRow to open the owning Collection's CollectionDetail.

Drop a pin, open AddLocationToCollection, pick *New Collection* to create one mid-flow, finish the editor, land back on MapOverview with the candidate auto-committed against the just-created Collection, then tap the post-add Snackbar to author the Review. The CollectionEditor detour preserves the in-flight candidate in the MapOverview host's UiState; DONE_AS_DRAFT_RETURN is modeled as a distinct event from DONE because the schema's one-transition-per-event constraint cannot branch on `return-to-draft-context`.
From the map, drill into a Collection, open one of its Entries, edit the review, submit, land back on the Entry detail with the review now saved.
